issues.legal_issue: A purchaser seeking possession may prove a sale deed without examining an attesting witness or the vendor when the deed’s execution is otherwise established.
material_facts: The purchaser sued for possession, relying on a registered sale deed from a housing society.
The defendant admitted the society’s title and did not object when the sale deed was admitted in evidence.
The purchaser testified and proved the execution of the sale deed.
The defendant’s plea of title by adverse possession had been found unproved.
issues.conclusion: The sale deed was duly proved and could support a decree for possession; the appeal was dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 54 of the Transfer of Property Act, 1882, a sale deed does not require attestation. Section 68 of the Evidence Act, 1872, therefore does not require an attesting witness to prove its execution. This differs from a gift deed, which Section 123 of the Transfer of Property Act requires to be attested by at least two witnesses. On the facts, the purchaser’s testimony establishing execution, the admission of the vendor’s title, and the absence of an objection when the deed was exhibited supported the finding that the deed was proved; neither an attesting witness nor the vendor had to be examined.

rule.if: civil_possession_suit and plaintiff_relies_on_sale_deed and vendor_title_admitted and plaintiff_testified_to_execution and no_objection_to_exhibiting_deed

predicates.civil_possession_suit: The plaintiff brought a civil suit seeking possession of property from a person said to be occupying it without authority.
predicates.plaintiff_relies_on_sale_deed: The plaintiff relied on a sale deed as the basis of the claimed title to the property.
predicates.vendor_title_admitted: The defendant admitted the title of the person or entity that conveyed the property to the plaintiff.
predicates.plaintiff_testified_to_execution: The plaintiff testified and established that the sale deed had been executed.
predicates.no_objection_to_exhibiting_deed: The defendant did not object when the sale deed was presented as evidence.

issues.definition: When a plaintiff seeks possession on the basis of a sale deed, the vendor’s title is admitted, the plaintiff establishes execution by testimony, and the defendant does not object to the deed being presented as evidence, the deed is proved and may support a possession decree.
